title: Gambling Apocalypse Kaiji
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In recession-era Japan, the jobless, idle Kaiji Itou is held liable for a friend's loan he co-signed. The loan shark Endou pushes him onto the gambling ship Espoir, where one night of rigged-rule games could clear the debt and losing means forced labor (MangaUpdates description; SKJAM review). Later arcs raise the stakes into life-or-death games run by the wealthy (AniList tags Death Game, Class Struggle).
life_message: Cunning, nerve and loyalty to fellow strugglers can carry a down-and-out man through a system rigged by the rich, though trust is costly.

content.note: Death games and 'implied torture' (SKJAM); AniList Death Game, Survival; MU Sadistic Character/s.
Sustained life-or-debt stakes and mind games; AniList Survival (94), Tragedy; MU Mind Games, Manipulation.

Gambling and debt drive the plot (AniList Gambling 100; SKJAM: co-signing, loan sharks); losses are ruinous.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Kaiji's pride and resentment push him to answer challenges personally (AniList description).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Games run outside the Coast Guard zone, beyond ordinary law (SKJAM).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Kaiji seeks allies among strangers, and trust is repeatedly betrayed (SKJAM; MU Manipulation).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: The rich hold power over debtors; story sides with those below (AniList Class Struggle).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Strategy and probability, not faith or custom, decide fates (MU Strategic Minds).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Debt, unemployment and survival dominate (MU Debt/s, Unemployment).

folkways.japan: Set in 1990s recession Japan, it reflects concern over unemployment, loan sharks and the shame of debt in a society that prizes steady work.

delivery.evidence: SKJAM describes the plot's desperation and rigged rules but no lecturing (to verify).

Predatory lending; the poor as prey

delivery.note: The critique of the wealthy is carried by the games' rules and outcomes; whether any rich character voices a lecture on 'winners and losers' was not checked.

winners_losers: The wealthy organizers profit while debtors are crushed; Kaiji survives by wits at great cost. Sympathy lies with the exploited, and greed and betrayal are shown as ruinous.
